Looking at the three culture conditions in the linear‑scale histograms (panels A, C, E), the distribution of sheath lengths shifts progressively to the right. In microfiber culture (A) most sheaths are <40 µm with a tail only to ~80 µm; in DRG neuron culture (C) the tail extends to ~90 µm; but in cerebellar slice culture (E) there is a large fraction of sheaths in the 30–80 µm range and a clear tail extending out to >120 µm. Thus, for a given oligodendrocyte, being cultured in a cerebellar slice most strongly predicts a longer myelinated sheath.

[ANSWER]C[/ANSWER]
